episode_title: Don’t Close the Academy - What business can learn from elite sport in the AI era

real_qa.q: Why should businesses invest in talent development and academy programs even when business performance is strong, similar to Premier League clubs?
real_qa.r: If businesses stop investing in their talent pipeline when the team is performing well and winning, things become very expensive in five years. If you cannot source, develop and retain talent in-house, you either have to bring it in externally at higher cost or your performance will plummet because you lack the people power and talent to deliver.
real_qa.requete: talent pipeline business development like Premier League

real_qa.q: What is bench depth and how should corporate workforce planning adopt this sports concept?
real_qa.r: Bench depth comes from basketball and refers to your depth chart across positions—knowing who your first, second and third option is at each role, and what happens if someone gets injured or underperforms. This principle from sports is starting to move into corporate workforce planning to ensure organizations have sufficient talent backup.

real_qa.q: How much time should senior leaders invest weekly in their own development to improve performance in corporate roles?
real_qa.r: If senior leaders mentally engage with work for approximately 50 hours per week, investing just half an hour to one hour per week—roughly 1-2 percent of that time—into planning, reflecting and self-improvement can yield 10 to 20 percent better output and communication with teams.
real_qa.requete: how much time self-improvement senior leaders weekly

real_qa.q: Why do elite sports teams spend disproportionately more time on training than on actual competition?
real_qa.r: Elite athletes train for a disproportionately high amount compared to how much and how long they actually compete. They keep their health front and center, adapt rather than work harder under stress, and focus on being in peak condition for brief competitive moments, which contrasts sharply with corporate environments.
real_qa.requete: elite athletes training versus competition time ratio

real_qa.q: What percentage of sports staff roles are poorly paid relative to the value they deliver?
real_qa.r: From a staff perspective for non-elite athletes in sports, approximately 95 percent of roles are not well paid relative to the actual value and impact that people deliver, despite long hours and weekends with minimal work-life balance.
real_qa.requete: sports staff pay compensation poorly paid

real_quote: People do things for different reasons. Some people pay the mortgage. Some people do it to get out of the house. Some people do it because it occupies their brain and they need that sort of stimulation.
key_stats: Approximately 95 percent of sports staff roles (non-elite athlete perspective) are not well paid relative to the value delivered
Player earning estimate in Premier League bottom-five team: 40,000 to 50,000 pounds per week
Annual compensation for relegated player: 2 to 3 million pounds per year despite poor performance
Senior leaders mental engagement: approximately 50 hours per week minimum
Recommended weekly development time investment: 0.5 to 1 hour out of 50-hour week (1-2 percent)
